title: Finite-limit closure through quasi-compact subobjects of coherent generators
statement: Let $\mathcal E=\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$ be a category of set sheaves on a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], with the universe convention [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $(G_i)_{i\in I}$ be a small generating family of quasi-compact objects [def-trf-coherent-topos]: every object receives an epimorphism from a coproduct of its members. Assume that $G_j\times_{G_i}G_k$ is quasi-compact for every $i,j,k$ and every pair of sheaf morphisms $G_j\to G_i$, $G_k\to G_i$. Then every $G_i$ is coherent. Suppose in addition that the terminal object is isomorphic to a member of the family and that, for every $i,j\in I$, $G_i\times G_j$ is isomorphic to a member. Let $\mathcal D$ consist of all objects $T$ admitting a monomorphism $T\hookrightarrow G_i$ for some $i$, with $T$ quasi-compact. Every object of $\mathcal D$ is coherent, and $\mathcal D$ is closed under finite limits, including limits of diagrams with arbitrary sheaf morphisms. There exists a small full subcategory containing the $G_i$, consisting of coherent objects and closed under chosen finite limits up to isomorphism. In particular every object in the finite-limit closure of the family is coherent; if the family generates $\mathcal E$ (every object receives an epimorphism from a coproduct of its members), that small subcategory is generating.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaf-sets-limits-sectionwise], all finite limits used below exist as limits of sheaves and are computed sectionwise. In particular products have tuple sections and pullbacks have pairs of sections with equal images. Quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness [def-trf-coherent-topos] are invariant under isomorphism: composing a jointly epimorphic family with an isomorphism preserves and reflects joint epimorphy by cancellation, and composing maps to an isomorphic target identifies their pullback universal properties. We may therefore use any chosen representatives of the stated products, terminal object and pullbacks.

source.place: Tag 00W2 (lemma-limit-sheaf); elementary transport of the definitions along isomorphisms.

proof.text: Every quasi-compact object $B$ has a finite jointly epimorphic family $(G_{j_a}\to B)_{a\in A}$. Indeed, generation supplies an epimorphism $\coprod_{a\in A_0}G_{j_a}\to B$ with a small index set $A_0$; the definition of quasi-compactness [def-trf-coherent-topos] selects a finite subset $A\subseteq A_0$ with epimorphic coproduct map. The same argument applies independently to any quasi-compact $C$. Empty selected families are allowed.

source.place: Tag 0D07 (definition-quasi-compact-topos), applied to the assumed generating covers.

proof.text: Fix $i$ and quasi-compact $B,C$ with arbitrary maps to $G_i$. Choose the finite generator covers of step 2. Clause (1) of [lem-trf-topos-finite-cover-calculus] makes $(G_{j_a}\times_{G_i}G_{k_b}\to B\times_{G_i}C)_{(a,b)\in A\times B_0}$ jointly epimorphic, where $B_0$ indexes the cover of $C$. Every source is quasi-compact by the assumed quasi-compactness of $G_j\times_{G_i}G_k$ for every pair of maps from generators, applied to the composite maps to $G_i$. The finite-family conclusion of clause (3) gives quasi-compactness of $B\times_{G_i}C$, including when an indexing set is empty. This proves quasi-separatedness of $G_i$ [def-trf-coherent-topos]; its assumed quasi-compactness now makes it coherent. No terminal-object or product-closure hypothesis has been used.

source.place: Tags 0GMP (lemma-image-of-quasi-compact), 0GMQ (lemma-coproduct-quasi-compact); finite-cover pullback calculus and the definition of quasi-separatedness.

proof.text: Let $m:T\hookrightarrow G_i$ be monic with $T$ quasi-compact. For quasi-compact $B,C$ and maps $b:B\to T$, $c:C\to T$, the objects $B\times_T C$ and $B\times_{G_i}C$ are canonically isomorphic: for any test sheaf $Z$, a pair $x:Z\to B$, $y:Z\to C$ satisfies $mbx=mcy$ exactly when $bx=cy$, by cancellation against $m$. This gives inverse maps by the two pullback universal properties, respecting projections. Since $G_i$ is quasi-separated by step 3, this pullback is quasi-compact. Thus $T$ is quasi-separated and hence coherent [def-trf-coherent-topos]. This proves the assertion about every object of $\mathcal D$.

source.place: Elementary monomorphism cancellation and pullback universal properties; definition of quasi-separatedness.

proof.text: Now impose the additional terminal and product hypotheses. The terminal object $1$ belongs to $\mathcal D$ via an isomorphism to a generator and is quasi-separated by step 3. For any quasi-compact $T,S$, the product $T\times S=T\times_1S$ is therefore quasi-compact [def-trf-coherent-topos]. If $T\hookrightarrow G_i$ and $S\hookrightarrow G_j$, the product map $T\times S\to G_i\times G_j$ is monic: equality after it implies equality of the two components by each given monomorphism, hence equality by the product universal property. Composing with the assumed isomorphism $G_i\times G_j\simeq G_k$ embeds $T\times S$ into a generator. Consequently $\mathcal D$ contains $1$ and is closed under binary products, and these products are coherent by step 4. Induction gives finite products, with the empty product $1$.

source.place: Elementary application of quasi-separatedness of the terminal object and product universal properties.

proof.text: For arbitrary sheaf maps $f,g:T\rightrightarrows S$ with $T,S\in\mathcal D$, put $Q=T\times S$ and let $a=(1_T,f)$ and $b=(1_T,g):T\to Q$ be their graphs. By step 5, $Q\in\mathcal D$, so $Q$ is quasi-separated by step 4. Both copies of $T$ are quasi-compact; hence $E=T\times_{a,Q,b}T$ is quasi-compact [def-trf-coherent-topos]. Its two projections to $T$ agree because the first components of $a,b$ are identities. Their common value $e:E\to T$ equalizes $f,g$. Conversely, any $h:Z\to T$ with $fh=gh$ gives the unique pullback map with both components $h$, proving that $e$ is an equalizer. It is monic since a map into $E$ is determined by these two equal components. Composing $e$ with $T\hookrightarrow G_i$ proves $E\in\mathcal D$. This argument applies to every $f,g$, without site-arrow representatives.

source.place: Elementary graph-pullback computation of the equalizer, using quasi-separatedness of the product.

proof.text: For a finite diagram $F:J\to\mathcal E$ with all $F(j)\in\mathcal D$, set $P=\prod_{j\in\operatorname{Ob}J}F(j)$ and $R=\prod_{\alpha:j\to k\in\operatorname{Mor}J}F(k)$. There are two maps $u,v:P\rightrightarrows R$ whose $\alpha$-components are $F(\alpha)\pi_j$ and $\pi_k$. By steps 5 and 6 their equalizer $L$ belongs to $\mathcal D$. A map $Z\to L$ is precisely a family $z_j:Z\to F(j)$ satisfying $F(\alpha)z_j=z_k$ for every arrow, so it is precisely a cone, uniquely. Thus $L$ is the diagram's limit. For the empty diagram $P=R=1$ and $L\simeq1$. Isomorphic choices stay in $\mathcal D$ by step 1. This proves closure under all finite limits, including diagrams with arbitrary sheaf morphisms.

source.place: Elementary product/equalizer construction of a finite limit; existence of products and equalizers established in steps 1, 5 and 6.

proof.text: To obtain a small full subcategory, start with the set $S_0=\{G_i:i\in I\}\cup\{1\}$. Recursively let $S_{n+1}$ contain $S_n$, one chosen product for each pair in $S_n$, and one chosen equalizer for each parallel pair of arrows between objects of $S_n$. These choices exist by step 1. Each $S_n$ is small in the containing universe [def-weil-size-convention]: a natural transformation between fixed sheaves $A,B$ is a family in the set $\prod_{U\in\operatorname{Ob}\mathcal C}\operatorname{Maps}(A(U),B(U))$ satisfying naturality equations [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], so all the arrow pairs used at each stage form a set. The countable union $S=\bigcup_{n\geq0}S_n$ is still small. Inductively every object of $S_n$ lies in $\mathcal D$ by steps 5 and 6. The full subcategory on $S$ therefore consists of coherent objects, contains the given generators, and is closed under chosen terminal objects, binary products and equalizers: finitely many input objects occur together at some stage. Step 7 then supplies its chosen finite limits up to isomorphism. The assumed generator epimorphisms remain generator epimorphisms from its objects, so it is generating. Finally $\mathcal D$ contains the family and is closed under finite limits and isomorphisms; hence every object obtained by finite-limit closure of the family is coherent.

source.place: Elementary countable finite-limit closure construction in the containing universe; small-site natural transformations are bounded by a product of function sets.

split_report.summary: Q84 supplies an eight-step proof using existing finite-cover calculus and the existing Mathlib leaf for sectionwise set-sheaf limits.
